description:
Blocks Enum sort_by/max/max_by/min/min_by/min_max/min_max_by (20 pairs), List.keysort, and the O(n log n) sort-then-group strategy that fz's flat-array Map needs.

VERIFIED at 67e09d373:
  fz:      Enum.sort(["pear", "apple", "fig"])  =>  ["pear", "fig", "apple"]
  Elixir:  Enum.sort(["pear", "apple", "fig"])  =>  ["apple", "fig", "pear"]

It does not error -- it silently produces a wrong ordering. Enum.sort/1 is
'fn (l, r) -> l <= r end', and <, <=, >, >= are numeric-only (ir_interp/binop.rs:21
does as_float().ok_or_else(|| "lhs is not numeric"); native uses IntCC/FloatCC at
prim.rs:1759).

Erlang defines a total order across all terms:
  number < atom < reference < fun < port < pid < tuple < map < list < bitstring

Needs a runtime fz_term_cmp primitive (non-allocating, returns i64) and a decision
about whether <=/< on mixed terms adopt term order or stay numeric-only with a
separate comparison entry point.
title: There is no term ordering: Enum.sort is silently wrong on non-numerics
